Reproducibility is less a technique than a habit: a set of small, unglamorous
practices that, taken together, let someone else — including your future self —
rebuild a result from its inputs. This short volume collects three such habits, one
per chapter, each written by a different contributor.

The chapters were
commissioned independently; the editor has imposed only a common notation and the
shared checklist reproduced in the appendix.

Provenance turns a result into a reproducible one by making its derivation explicit.

is deliberately strong: a partial record that omits a
transformation is not provenance, because the artifact cannot be rebuilt from it. The
recommended practice, following

In practice the record is emitted by the pipeline tool itself, so
that provenance cannot drift out of sync with the computation it describes.
The contributors agreed on a short checklist, applicable regardless of tooling:
every result traces to a version-controlled commit;
every figure regenerates from a script, not by hand;
every notebook passes restart-and-run-all in CI;
every derived artifact carries a provenance record.
A result that satisfies all four can be rebuilt by a stranger.

The checklist
is intentionally tool-agnostic; the chapters give one concrete realisation of each
item, but others are possible.
